chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'the nature made by God upon which He has created people' (30:30).
He said: He created them all upon tawhid (Divine Unity/Oneness).

key_terms.التَّوْحِيد: Tawhid — Divine Unity/Oneness; the foundational doctrine that God is one and unique, with no partners or associates
key_terms.فَطَرَ: Fatara — to create, to originate; specifically creating something according to a primordial pattern or constitution
key_terms.فِطْرَة: Fitrah — the primordial, God-given nature or disposition of every human being; the innate constitution at creation

ai.seo_question: What does 'fitrah' mean in the Quran and hadith? What is the innate nature of humans according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith records Zurara's question to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the Quranic concept of 'fitrah' — the primordial nature instilled in all human beings at creation (Quran 30:30). The Imam interprets this verse definitively: the innate disposition God built into every person is tawhid, the recognition of divine unity. This hadith was central to early Shia theological debates about human nature, affirming that monotheism is not merely taught but is intrinsic to the human soul.
